chunks: O believers, fear God and forego the interest that is owing, if you really believe.

key_terms.اتَّقُوا: Fear God or be conscious of God (taqwa)
key_terms.الرِّبَا: Usury or interest, specifically the excess charged on loans
key_terms.مُبْقِي: Remaining or what is left over

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'forego the interest that is owing' in Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often viewed as the final stage of the gradual prohibition of riba, commanding believers to retain only the principal amount after deducting interest, thereby serving as a definitive test of sincerity in faith. It underscores the inseparable link between economic justice and spiritual integrity, a theme emphasized by Imams who highlight that abandoning riba is a prerequisite for divine acceptance of worship. This commandment not only purifies wealth but also establishes a moral economy rooted in equity and mercy.
